newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caldera to announce Venezuela wage bonus Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Caldera to announce Venezuela wage bonus Wednesday.

text.p: Venezuelan President Rafael Caldera said he will announce a so-called "bridging bonus" for private sector workers on Wednesday because Congress had not yet finished discussions of pending law reforms.

"Since discussions in Congress are taking time ... we're going to grant a transport and food bonus that will contribute to substantially increase the minimum legal wage," he said at a ceremony at Miraflores presidential palace.
Caldera gave no figures but said the bonus would be automatically converted into salary once the wide-ranging Labor Law reforms were adopted by Congress.

The government has not officially said what the wage increase would be but government officals and political sources said the raise would take the minimum wage to between 68,000 and $75,000 bolivars ($142-156) per month from the current 53,000, including bonuses.
Caldera said he had no intention to greet workers on Labor Day "empty-handed" and noted that a 70 percent increase was agreed for public sector workers in February.
He said the bonus issue would be discussed and approved during the weekly cabinet meeting Wednesday morning.
Presidential sources said Caldera would probably explain it to Venezuelans in a radio and television address in the evening.
